issues: Integrity: nothing found. The diff does not read files, use the network, paste coordinates, or touch the harness. The harness raised no integrity flags.

The change does nothing. It adds SCREEN_ITER, BATCH_SIZE and TOP_K, but nothing in the diff uses them. The new maxiter parameter of _solve_once defaults to MAX_ITER, and no call site passes a different value. So the candidate behaves exactly like the incumbent: the screening/batch/top-k idea the constants suggest was never wired in. The edit is unused code, which goes against 'simpler is better', and it should not be kept as is.

The numbers fit a no-op. The candidate ran once and scored -2.6261 against the incumbent's mean of -2.6280 over 10 runs. The gap of 0.0019 is within the noise, since one run has an sd of about 0.0023. Rejecting it is right, but the run tells us nothing about the screening idea, because that idea was never run.

z checks out. With sd = 0.0023, SE = 0.0023 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/10) ≈ 0.00241, so z = (-2.6280 - (-2.6261)) / 0.00241 ≈ -0.79. That matches the reported -0.793; the small difference comes from the values being rounded to 4 decimals.

Note: this job used a slot to test a change that alters nothing. If the screening idea is wanted, the next try should actually do the screening (run many short SLSQP solves with maxiter=SCREEN_ITER, then refine the TOP_K best).
